sections.presenting_complaint: Cough and coryza for 4 days, increased work of breathing since yesterday.
sections.history: Coryza and cough for 4 days; fast breathing since yesterday. Temperature up to 37.9 °C. Feeding most of his usual amount. Four wet nappies in 24 hours (usually 6–7). Has had an apnoea. No cyanosis. Small posset after coughing. Born at 39 weeks, no neonatal problems. No cardiac or respiratory history. Immunisations up to date.
sections.medications_allergies: Paracetamol once yesterday. No known drug allergies.
sections.examination: Temperature 37.8 °C. RR 54, HR 150, SpO2 95% in air. Mild subcostal recession. CRT under 2 seconds. Alert. Bilateral fine crackles and wheeze.
sections.impression: Bronchiolitis with moderately reduced feeding; borderline for referral (feeds about 50%). Managed at home with early review.
sections.plan: Small, frequent feeds; saline nose drops before feeds. Advised illness may worsen over days 3–5. Clinical review tomorrow morning.
sections.safety_netting: Call 999 if pauses in breathing, blue colour, or severe difficulty breathing. Call GP or 111 urgently if feeds fall below half, no wet nappy for 12 hours, or more tired or floppy.
